propositions: The LLM judge's Per-finding Pass-3 decision exhibits drift across repeated runs on the same input; Exp A measures self-consistency via Fleiss' κ ≥0.6 AND raw agreement ≥0.8 over N=50 findings × 3 votes drawn from the G6/E4/T3 cohort.

Section-order permutation of the plan input causes the gate verdict to flip between {PASS, BLOCK, INDETERMINATE} across orderings; Exp B measures order-shuffle stability via Fleiss' κ ≥0.6 AND raw agreement ≥0.8 over N=14 plans × 3 distinct permutations.

Infra-level INDETERMINATE verdicts carrying coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed are execution failures and must be excluded-and-re-run; only genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (neither flag set) counts as a stable outcome category.

E6 re-judges existing, frozen, reproducible samples without treating any judge output as ground truth, measuring only stochastic agreement across repeated runs — this is distinct from E1's descoped circular-adjudication error and does not require TP/FP labels.

E6's two passing floors (Exp A and Exp B) are gating prerequisites for R5 (asserted_capability_confirmed) and R3 (new container criterion), respectively; a sub-floor result blocks the dependent story.
